fix: A bare adjective in a list that begins 'leaflets ...' belongs to the leaflets, not to the whole leaf. Carry the subject of the list forward to every item in it.
reason: 'reticulate-veined' sits in the leaflet list ('leaflets 2 pairs ..., obovate, ..., reticulate-veined'). The quality (reticulate venation) is right, but it is said of the leaflets.

fix: In a leaf description, 'obtuse or acute' after the outline shape and before the size refers to the tip, as in the usual 'base ..., apex ...' order. Map obtuse/acute without a named part to the leaf apex.
reason: Botanically, 'obtuse or acute' describes the tip of the leaf, not the outline of the whole blade, which is given separately as elliptic to sub-orbicular.

fix: 'Branchlet' and 'twig' are synonyms of PO branch (PO_0025073). Use branch, not the general stem class.
reason: The colour range purple to gray is said of the branchlets, not of the stem as a whole. The colour values and the continuum reading are right.
The flora says the flowers are solitary or paired in the axils. The arrangement of flowers as solitary or paired, as alternatives, matches.
'Stem densely branched at base' becomes 'stem base, branched'. The modifier 'densely' is lost, but the annotation is still true.

fix: With 'Petals 3, unequal; upper two ..., ovate, lower linear', each shape belongs to a different group of petals. The position slot (upper / lower) must be kept.
reason: Only the upper two petals are ovate; the lower petal is linear. 'Petal ovate' without the position contradicts the lower petal.
The raceme has numerous flowers. 'Flower present, many' is true. The missing link to the inflorescence does not make the statement false.

fix: When the flora writes 'apex <shape>' after the leaf, the bearer is the leaf apex, not the leaf blade. The named part was dropped.
reason: The flora names the apex explicitly ('apex obtuse or acute'), but the annotation puts the shape on the whole leaf blade.

fix: In 'base <shape>', the named part 'base' must become the bearer (leaf base), the same way 'apex' should become leaf apex.
reason: Sagittate or auriculate is said of the base of the stem leaves, not of the whole leaf. Sagittate is PATO_0001881 'arrow-shaped' and auriculate is PATO_0001981, so the values are right.

'Umbellets many-flowered' becomes 'flowers present, many', inside a second-order inflorescence (the umbellet). That matches.

fix: When a part of the seed (raphe) is named after a semicolon, it must be the bearer. Do not fall back to the seed named in the earlier clause.
reason: Only the raphe is tuberculate. The seed surfaces are striate, so 'seed tuberculate' is wrong.

reason: The flora says the capsule is subtruncate only at the apex, while the capsule as a whole is globose. 'Fruit truncated' without the place clashes with 'globose'.
